props.title: Your course updates itself when your sources change
props.intro: Edit a doc or merge to a repo. ulams finds every lesson and question that cites it and proposes the update. You approve, and learners keep their progress.
props.valueLine: Courses stop going stale, and nothing changes without your approval.
props.description: An animated example in three steps. First, a line in docs/slo.md changes from 99.9 % to 99.95 % and a new line about the 30-day budget is added. Second, ulams finds the lesson paragraph and the quiz question that cite docs/slo.md section 2. Third, a proposal with a red and green diff appears, the author clicks Approve, the lesson text updates and a badge confirms that learner progress was kept.

props.title: Build a course from a document in minutes
props.intro: Drop in a runbook, answer three questions, and review a cited outline and drafts before anything goes live.
props.valueLine: From a PDF to a published, cited course, with you approving every step.
props.description: An animated example of the studio course builder. A file named incident-runbook.pdf is dropped in, three interview answers appear (engineers, 45 minutes, a quiz per lesson), an outline of three modules and five lessons grows with a source chip on each lesson, one lesson streams in with citations, a quiz question cites its source, an example cost counter reaches 18 cents, and Apply publishes the course.

lesson.title: Severity levels
lesson.text: Sev 1 means customers cannot check out. Page the on-call lead and open an incident channel straight away.

props.title: Your brand, your academy, one course per source
props.intro: Bring your style and your content. ulams gives you a branded academy on its own subdomain, a separate cited course for every source, and the learner analytics for each of them.
props.valueLine: Your look, your subdomain, your content, and clear numbers per course.
props.description: An animated example in four steps. One: an agent such as Claude Code, with the ulams CLI and the Figma or Stitch MCP attached, reads a design (a Figma file, a Stitch DESIGN.md, a brand guide PDF or a logo and colours), extracts colours, fonts, logo and corner radius, and runs ulams theme set and ulams settings set; a custom front built on the headless API is shown as the alternative. Two: a themed academy appears on its own subdomain, acme.ulams.app, with a landing page, a course catalogue and an admin, all in the extracted brand. Three: documents, PDFs, a Git repository and a web page each become their own cited course, built by the course builder and kept in sync by Living Course. Four: a per-course dashboard shows learner progress, quiz performance, learners at risk and the sections that confuse people. All names and values are an example.

props.title: An LMS that earns trust
props.intro: Built for developer and customer education: content that changes with every release, sold and delivered to many audiences.

items.title: Living Course
items.text: Courses stay in sync with the docs and repos they come from, and adapt to each learner.

items.title: Cited by design
items.text: Every AI-generated element cites the source fragment it is based on. AI proposes, the author approves the diff.

items.title: A site per customer
items.text: Each tenant gets its own subdomain, theme and isolated database: white-label academies for customers and partners.

items.title: Self-hosted, open core
items.text: MIT-licensed core you can run on your own servers. Your content and learner data stay yours; no lock-in.

items.title: Standards first
items.text: H5P, SCORM, cmi5 and xAPI work today; the same course can be delivered anywhere. LTI 1.3 is next.

items.title: Commerce built in
items.text: Catalogue, checkout and subscriptions through a headless Sylius shop; access granted only from verified orders.

props.title: How a course keeps up with its sources
props.intro: The killer feature on our roadmap: when your docs change, the course proposes its own update, and you stay in control.

items.title: Connect sources
items.text: Point ulams at docs, repos and release notes. They become the only ground truth for the course.

items.title: Generate with citations
items.text: Lessons, quizzes and interactives are drafted from approved objectives, each element linked to its source fragment.

items.title: Review diffs when sources change
items.text: A change upstream becomes an update proposal: a reviewable diff you approve, edit or reject.

final.intro: The killer feature: when your docs change, the course proposes its own update, and you stay in control.

props.title: Six academies, one platform
props.intro: Each demo is a separate tenant with its own theme, course and data, running on the same ulams install. Open it as a learner or step into its admin.
props.note: Demos reset every hour. No sign-up: you are logged in automatically.

props.title: Delivered anywhere
props.intro: Standards over lock-in: bring existing packages, track learning anywhere, integrate through the API.
